description: STEM is a finite-element model from the StemVibrations developers for railway-induced vibrations. It couples train-track interaction to wave propagation through the subsoil using Kratos Multiphysics. Users define track and soil geometry, material properties, vehicle motion, loads and boundary conditions through Python. The software provides two-dimensional and three-dimensional meshes, linear elastic soils and an interface for other material models, along with implicit or explicit time integration. Results can be written to JSON and VTK for analysis and visualization. Spatial extent, mesh resolution and simulation duration depend on the study configuration. Source code, tutorials and a PyPI package are public and free under BSD-3-Clause. These tools support railway design and comparisons of vibration-mitigation measures. A limitation is that soil and vehicle assumptions require appropriate parameterization; analytical benchmarks do not establish accuracy at every field site. Python 3.10 to 3.12 is documented, and ParaView is recommended for viewing results. No directly related existing catalogue record was established. The model was not installed or run.
inputs: Train and track geometry, speed and irregularities
Soil layers, material properties and spatial variability
Boundary conditions, loads and time-integration settings
